title: Pesce Spada alla Ghiotta
author: Marco Bellini
desc: Swordfish steaks braised in a bold Sicilian sauce of tomato, olives, capers, and celery, the name meaning 'greedy style' for how thoroughly the sauce is meant to be enjoyed.
longDesc: This preparation from the Strait of Messina, where swordfish is prized above almost any other fish, braises the steaks gently in a briny, herbaceous sauce rather than grilling them, resulting in tender fish infused throughout with bold Sicilian flavor.
ingredients: 2 tbsp raisins, soaked in warm water
80 ml (1/3 cup) extra virgin olive oil
steps: Warm the olive oil in a large pan and saute the onion and celery until softened.
Add the crushed tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the olives, capers, drained raisins, and pine nuts, and simmer for another 5 minutes.
Season the swordfish steaks and nestle them into the sauce.
Cover and cook gently for 10-12 minutes, turning once, until the fish is just cooked through.
Finish with fresh basil and serve hot with plenty of sauce.
chefTips: Braising the swordfish gently in the sauce keeps it moist, unlike grilling, which can dry it out quickly.
The sweet-savory combination of raisins and olives is a hallmark of Sicilian cooking - don't be tempted to omit either.
Fresh swordfish steaks, not previously frozen if possible, give the best texture.
commonMistakes: Overcooking the swordfish, which dries out quickly even when braised.
Using a thin, underseasoned sauce that doesn't stand up to the rich fish.
Skipping the sweet elements (raisins), missing the dish's characteristic Sicilian balance.
reheating: Reheat gently on the stovetop, taking care not to overcook the fish further.
healthBenefits: Swordfish is a good source of lean protein and vitamin D.
culturalNote: Pesce spada alla ghiotta is closely tied to the Strait of Messina, an area renowned for its swordfish fishing tradition and season each spring and summer.
